facts: Meghji Pethraj Shah Medical College was established by the then Government of Saurashtra at Jamnagar in the year 1955.
For establishing the college, Shri M.P. Shah donated a sum of Rupees fifteen lakhs subject to certain conditions.
The government hospital then known as Irwin Hospital was attached to the said college to meet the requirement of a hospital with necessary bed-strength.

In the year 1993, the Government of Gujarat repudiated one of the conditions attached to the donation, which led the M.P. Shah Charitable Trust to approach the Gujarat High Court for issuance of a writ commanding the State of Gujarat to continue to abide by the said condition.
The medical college was accordingly established and started functioning from June 1955 with a strength of 60 students.
As per the arrangement contained in the aforesaid letters, Shri M.P. Shah was permitted to nominate students for admission to the extent of 10% of the total strength obtaining at a given time.
In course of time, the college and the hospital grew in strength and size.
From the year 1964-65, therefore, only 12 students were being nominated by the trust.
issues: Whether the Government of Gujarat was justified in repudiating one of the conditions attached to the donation made by Shri M.P. Shah for establishing Meghji Pethraj Shah Medical College.
Whether the respondent-trust acquiesced in the decision of the Government of Gujarat to discontinue the 12 donor seats in M.P. Shah Medical College, Jamnagar.
petitioner_arguments: The arrangement between the then Government of Saurashtra and Shri M.P. Shah was not binding upon the Government of Gujarat.
The respondent-trust acquiesced in the decision of the Government of Gujarat to discontinue the 12 donor seats in M.P. Shah Medical College, Jamnagar.
respondent_arguments: The arrangement between the then Government of Saurashtra and Shri M.P. Shah was binding upon the Government of Gujarat.
The respondent-trust did not acquiesce in the decision of the Government of Gujarat to discontinue the 12 donor seats in M.P. Shah Medical College, Jamnagar.
court_reasoning: The arrangement between the then Government of Saurashtra and Shri M.P. Shah was not binding upon the Government of Gujarat.
The respondent-trust acquiesced in the decision of the Government of Gujarat to discontinue the 12 donor seats in M.P. Shah Medical College, Jamnagar.
holding: The Court held that the arrangement between the then Government of Saurashtra and Shri M.P. Shah was not binding upon the Government of Gujarat.
The respondent-trust did not acquiesce in the decision of the Government of Gujarat to discontinue the 12 donor seats in M.P. Shah Medical College, Jamnagar.
